title: How proprietary formats have become Microsoft’s main tool for lock-in
summary: This article from The Document Foundation (LibreOffice developers) analyzes how Microsoft strategically uses proprietary file formats as a primary mechanism for customer lock-in, making it difficult for users to migrate to alternative office productivity solutions.
problem_solved: Examines how proprietary file formats create artificial switching costs that keep users locked into Microsoft's ecosystem.
why_valuable: Raises awareness about the anti-competitive implications of proprietary formats and highlights why open standards like ODF are important for user freedom and market competition.
